text: Hello everyone, welcome to the English class.Please get your student's book and the worksheet ready.Remember last lesson's homework?Some students have handed in their two verse poems.Let's enjoy Sam's work.And then one day I see him in the school where he works.He's speaking in the front of the classroom.He's talking about the secret of the mother nature.So interesting.He's teaching his students with his body language, quite energetic.He's making everyone down there listen to him carefully.So charming, not like me.He's a great man, my dad.I like Sam's poem.In the first verse, he writes about an ordinary and even boring father who follows the same routine every day.Quite familiar to you and me, right?Well, in the second verse, we see a change in the character.The author describes the scene where his dad works.Action words like speaking, talking about, teaching with body language, help us see a teacher, maybe a science teacher, giving lessons.Besides, adjectives and adverbs like so interesting, quite energetic, and carefully are properly used.They form a vivid picture in my mind.From the poem, we can feel the love Sam has for his father.Good job.Today, we're going to read another poem.Before reading, let's first look at a picture.What is the girl in the picture doing?She's playing with some little toys, isn't she?We can say, she's playing house, or playing pretend, 过家家.Did you ever play house when you were a young kid?Did you pretend yourself to be a superhero, a princess, a prince?I did.And when we play house, sometimes we play with pretend and play toys.For example,pretend and play doctor set,house family people dolls.What about the toys in this picture?Can you give the toy set a name?What about classroom or school?Pretend and play set.What's in the set that you're playing?What kind of scene is being described?It is a scene of a child playing and having lessons at a school.Take a closer look.See the two teachers giving lessons?What subjects do they teach?The man is a math teacher, and the lady is an English teacher.Playing pretend requires a lot of imagination.What do you think the girl imagined her two teachers to be?We'll find the answers out later.This is the title of the poem.Can you guess what the poem is mainly about?Yes, the girl's school, but a real school?And who is the speaker of the poem?Read through the poem and check your prediction.The girl's school, but a real school?Time's up, everyone.For the first question, to see whether it is about a real school, these two lines will show you the answer.It says that people are not real, they are little dolls, just toys.So it's about a toy school, but not a real one.Second, who is the speaker?Yes, this little girl, she is a student.Then comes the question, who is the speaker talking to?Think about it.Do you notice these words?Lee must be her teacher, so she's talking to her teacher, Ms.Now let's read the poem closely.Read verse one and find out why did the girl write the poem?Do you have the answer?From the first line, for your homework, write a poem.We know, it was her homework.Did she take the homework seriously?These two lines give us the answer.I wrote these verses on my own.On one's own means without anyone's help.So the girl wrote the poem without anyone's help, all by herself, independently.And be pleased with means be happy about.The girl hoped the teacher could be happy about the poem she handed in.From these lines, we can tell, yes, the girl took the homework quite seriously.Now let's move on to the next part, verses two to four.Read carefully and complete the table.Please do it on your worksheet, task one.Please do it on your worksheet.Time's up, boys and girls.This is Jane's work.Let's check the answers.In this part, a men teacher is introduced, Mr.Black.He is cross.You may have also found the word cross, You may have also found the word cross in verse three.But what does it mean?Here, cross is an adjective, which means very angry.What words can show Mr.Black is often cross?Silence, pay attention.It seems that students in his class are noisy and they don't pay attention.They don't listen to the teacher carefully or with interest.So Mr.Black scolded them.He spoke to the students angrily.Scold, ze be.Follow me, scold.Again, scold.And Mr.Black put pupils in detention.Detention is a punishment in which a student is required to stay at school after the rest of the students have left, 放学留堂.Put someone in detention, 法某人放学留堂, or get detention, 被留堂.For example, I got detention for being late for a class.Follow me, detention.Again, detention.These are the things Mr.Black does, which can happen very often.He appears to be very angry.The lady teacher is Ms.White.Let's read the descriptions for Ms.White first.White helped in every way.In every way means in all ways, in every part of the student's life.And she loved chatting.Chat means to talk in a friendly way, 闲聊.I guess Ms.White is willing to listen to her students.But there's one more detail in the verse.Her lessons seem like play.Play is a noun here.It shows her lessons probably have lots of games and activities, very fun to take.Do you like such lessons?Now let's go back to the opinion about Ms.Is kind a suitable word for Ms.I would say yes.Do you remember the question I raised when we talked about the picture earlier?What did the girl imagine her teachers to be?Now we've got the answer.She imagined that one of the teachers was rather cross, but the other was kind and friendly.The next thing I want to talk about is their names.What do their names suggest?Why are they called black and white?Let me show you something in the dictionary.Black actually has something to do with anger or hate.White means morally good.So, got it?Their names suggest one is often angry and students don't like him, while the other is a good teacher and is quite popular.Using black and white as names is a kind of word play.That's similar to Chinese.Hong lian is used to talk about a good person.Bai lian is for someone bad.Have you heard of them?One more question.What does the line, but Ms.White was like you, Ms.Li, suggest?Here the speaker compares Ms.White to Ms.So we know in the speaker's eyes, Ms.Li is also a good teacher just like Ms.Then we come to verse 5, which is the last verse of the poem.Read and think about what is the effect of verse 5.As we discussed before, when finishing reading this verse, we know that the school in verses 2 to 4 is not a real one.Verse 5 reveals the truth, 皆是真相.But there is something more.I wonder if you have noticed the beginning of the verse, if you are puzzled by my words.When you came to this line, did you have a question in mind?Any puzzling words before that?So this verse also encourages me to read back, to find something strange.Let's go back to verses 2 to 4 to find the puzzling words, shall we?Everyone, let me tell you what I'm thinking about.First, the little here.Little has the meaning of young at age.But after reading verse 5, we know that little here can mean small and short in size.And little boys and girls refers to small dolls.A tricky word, isn't it?The other is two teachers and a hall.Why only two teachers and a hall in a school?That's too puzzling.But remember the classroom pretend and play set?We saw only two toy teachers and a toy school hall, right?If you are a careful reader, before reaching the end of the poem, you may have already noticed these strange things.This is what we call suspense created by the writer.And since the truth will be revealed at last, this is also called a foreshadowing dropped by the writer.So far, we've read the whole poem closely.Please complete a dialogue about the poem My School.You can also find the task on your worksheet.Thank you for watching.Time's up.Jane's work is for your reference.For blank 2, you can also write toys.Angry means the same as cross.And for Miss White, helpful, friendly are also correct.But pay attention to the next blank.These answers are OK too, but the words in the blank should go with or should match the opinion word about Miss White.Imagine yourself being Miss Lee.When you read the girl's homework, how would you feel?Happy, right?Because the girl compared you to the kind and friendly Miss White in the poem.So, what feeling or experience is the author sharing?The answer is for your reference.The author describes two imaginary teachers and shows the love and respect for her real teacher, Miss Lee.Everyone, time to read the poem aloud.While you read, try to figure out the answers to these three questions.They will help you better understand the structure of the poem.Ready?My School.For your homework, write a poem.You said to us, Miss Lee, I wrote these verses on my own.I hope you're pleased with me.I want to talk about the school I loved when I was small.With lots of little boys and girls, two teachers and a hall.Black was sometimes cross.Silence!Pay attention!He scolded pupils in his class and put them in detention.But Miss White was like you, Miss Lee.She helped in every way.She loved chatting with her class.Her lessons seemed like play.Can you explain, Miss Lee?The staff and students were not real.They're little dolls, you see.Got the answers?How many verses are there in the poem?Five.How many lines are there in each verse?There are four.So we know that the number of lines in each verse is fixed.Is it a rhyming poem?The answer is yes.The rhyming words are Poem Ong.Leave me in the first verse.Small hall in the second verse.Cross class.Attention detention in the third verse.Way play in the fourth verse and Lee see in the last verse.But what if I make some changes to the poem?As we learned before, Ong my own means by myself.So what about replacing Ong my own with by myself?What if I replace small with young?Cross with angry?What if pay attention is put before silence?And you see in the last line is deleted?Read the new version aloud and think about the question.Do you have any idea?The original poem is a rhyming one with quite a few rhyming words.If all these rhyming words are replaced by other words, the poem will no longer rhyme.You won't find any rhyme in the poem.What if I replace by myself?The poem will no longer rhyme.You won't feel the same rhythm and even don't feel so energetic.Although the meaning remains the same, it will not have the same pleasant effect.So far we've learned three poems in this unit.Are they all rhyming poems?Does rhyme have anything to do with the subject of the poem?What is subject?It is the topic, the idea or thing that the poem talks about.Common subjects for poetry include nature, growing up, growing old, children and life events.The last thing we'll focus on is the rhyme and the subject of the poem.Now work on task 3.Complete the table on your worksheet.How's everything going?There's one poem among the three, which actually doesn't rhyme.My dad at home and my mom at home.My dad at home and at work.The other two have rhyme.The subject, never a dull moment, is a family and the home they live in.Do you remember in what way the author shares his feeling?Yes, in a funny way.For the next one, the subject is the speaker's dad.How does rhyme or the lack of it affect how we feel about the subject?Think about my dad at home and at work.Without rhyme, it sounds more natural, doesn't it?It's just like the speaker's talking to you.Telling you about what he sees and feels in life, making you feel the same and touched by the poem.Lack of rhyme expresses the thoughts and feelings about his dad in a natural way.It seems more heartfelt and is suitable for the subject of the poem.But for the other two rhyming poems, never a dull moment in my school.Don't you feel more energetic and positive when you read them?I think they are great to read aloud and evoke positive feelings from readers.They are suitable for the
